messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Morning all. Atlas release pipeline needs to be sorted this week. @lead please draft the deployment approach today.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Draft: we ship to a staging environment first, then promote to production behind a manual approval gate. No automated production deploys for now.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: I can add smoke tests to the staging step so the promotion gate has evidence to check.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Sounds good. Keep staging-first with a manual promote, and we revisit automated deploys later.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Environment check: the CI runner currently uses Node 20, but our test suite needs Node 22 globals.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Pin Node 22 everywhere, CI and container images included.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: I will add the version file and update the build image.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: @lead please acknowledge and record this as a project rule: no direct pushes to main, every change goes through a PR.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Acknowledged and recorded: no direct pushes to main, every change goes through a PR.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: I will wire branch protection so the rule is enforced, not just documented.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Timeline: release deadline is October 31, and the QA handoff starts one week earlier, on October 24.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Noted, October 31 release with QA handoff on October 24.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: I propose we containerize with Compose files and deploy that same file to production. Simpler than a pipeline.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Compose in production is fragile for us; we have no secrets story there. I would not go that way.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Agreed, rejected: production stays on the platform's native deploy pipeline, not a Compose deploy.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Update: the smoke tests are green on staging, and I propose a blue-green cutover for the first production release.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Let's go with blue-green for the first release; it gives us a clean instant rollback.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Housekeeping preference from me: I review diffs before 9am, so please land large PRs the evening before.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Understood, we will queue large PRs for the evening.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Staging smoke tests are still green after the Node 22 pin.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: I will prepare the release checklist, including the rollback steps.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Release checklist v1 is ready; rollback steps are included.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Rollback rehearsal passed today; recovery time was 4 minutes.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Rethink on blue-green: we do not have double capacity. I want a canary at 10% traffic instead.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Agreed, switching the plan to canary at 10% for production. I will update the checklist.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Checklist updated; the canary step sits before full traffic.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: What if we skipped staging entirely and promoted straight to canary?

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Too risky; staging catches config drift before real users see it.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Final check: staging and production images both run Node 22, and smoke tests are green.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Great. Code freeze aligns with the QA handoff on October 24, release is October 31.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Calendar invites sent for the freeze and release days.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: I will be on support rotation during release week.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Thanks everyone, that's a wrap for today.
